item.text: {"verdict":"request_changes","summary":"Four issues remain above nit severity: two gaps in the attested security boundary and two unsafe host-side operations.","recommendations":[{"severity":"blocking","location":"Container run configuration; Premises / non-self-calibrating policy validator; Security battery item 2","issue":"[P1] Process-namespace isolation is neither explicitly configured nor made mandatory. The validator lists capabilities, privileges, rootfs, logging, and networking, but does not reject host PID/IPC/UTS/cgroup namespace modes. A freshly fingerprinted `--pid=host` run could therefore pass; because the container uses the invoking host UID, a shell-denial regression could expose same-UID host process data through `/proc`, contradicting the claimed process boundary.","suggestion":"Require and inspect private PID, IPC, UTS, and cgroup namespaces and `Privileged=false`; also reject unconfined security profiles and unapproved device/device-cgroup requests. Include these values in the semantic profile and add negative live tests, including a host-PID same-UID canary."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"Premises / live-evidence manifest; Installer steps 2–5; SKILL.md Unix dispatch","issue":"[P1] Evidence is not bound to the host Python runtime that executes the security enforcement. `host_impl_digest` covers source files, while dispatch later resolves a mutable PATH entry named `python3`. An interpreter, standard-library, or dependency change can therefore leave evidence current even though different code now performs no-follow copying, credential handling, stream limiting, process cleanup, hashing, and durability operations.","suggestion":"Define the supported Python runtime, resolve and pin the executable used by dispatch, and fingerprint its implementation/version/build plus all runtime dependencies in the premise and live-evidence records. Prefer an immutable packaged runtime or versioned environment; invalidate evidence and rerun all gates whenever that execution substrate changes."},{"severity":"important","location":"Container lifecycle and verdict retrieval, steps 3–4","issue":"[P2] Bounding the read of an artifact after `docker cp` does not bound the copy itself. A normal `docker cp CONTAINER:path destination` materializes the complete file before validation, so an oversized verdict can consume host storage before the stated artifact limit is enforced.","suggestion":"Use a size-bounded transfer protocol, such as streaming `docker cp ... -` through a bounded tar parser into an owner-only temporary file, or validate the immutable post-Codex file size and still enforce a byte limit during transfer. Abort and clean up immediately on declared or actual over-limit data, and test host-side copy overflow."},{"severity":"important","location":"Installer & skill dispatch, step 7","issue":"[P2] Appending directly to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is not crash-safe, concurrency-safe, or symlink-safe. Interruption can leave a partial activation directive, concurrent installers can interleave or duplicate it, and following a user-controlled symlink can modify an unintended file.","suggestion":"Validate the destination with no-follow semantics, serialize updates, detect concurrent generations, write a complete sibling file while preserving intended metadata, durably flush it, and atomically replace the destination. Define failure ordering so an unsuccessful activation update leaves the prior configuration intact."}]}
